procedure.description: insertion of spinal neurostimulator pulse generator with connection to leads

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Northwind Mutual Health denied the claim for CPT 63685 (insertion of spinal neurostimulator pulse generator with connection to leads) with date of service 2026-01-30. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: Documentation does not establish a successful trial meeting the plan’s definition of 50 percent pain reduction with functional improvement.

criteria.text: Chronic intractable neuropathic pain of the trunk or limbs (such as failed back surgery syndrome or complex regional pain syndrome) for at least 6 months despite conservative therapy including medications, physical therapy, and injections.
Psychological evaluation documenting no untreated psychiatric condition or substance use disorder that would preclude benefit from neuromodulation.
A successful trial of at least 5 days with at least 50 percent pain reduction and documented functional improvement.
No further surgically correctable lesion identified on imaging.

chart.text: Knee pain going down stairs, left side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.
From the referring physician: please evaluate and treat as you see fit. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.
A1c came back 6.7. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. She is motivated.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 3.2, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 50. Repeat in a year.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 10 years.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.
Mammogram report forwarded for the record. Bilateral screening, BI-RADS 1, negative, routine screening in one year.
She called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in the spring. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.

53 year old woman in the pain clinic referred by her spine surgeon. Discussed spinal cord stimulation, what a trial involves, and that it is for leg-predominant neuropathic pain. She is interested. Her history otherwise: seasonal allergies. Allergies: sulfa, hives as a child. Does not smoke, a glass of wine on weekends, works from home. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Persistent bilateral leg and low back pain 18 months after an L4-S1 fusion, 8 out of 10 most days, burning quality down both legs. On gabapentin 1200 three times daily and duloxetine 60, 14 weeks of PT, two epidurals and a medial branch block without durable relief. Post-operative MRI and CT show a solid fusion, no recurrent stenosis, no hardware problem; the spine surgeon has nothing further to offer surgically.

Psychological evaluation for neuromodulation candidacy. PHQ-9 score 7, mild; no somatic symptom disorder; no substance use disorder, opioid use stable and monitored; realistic expectations about pain reduction rather than cure. Cleared for trial.
Work note requested for a sick day last Thursday. Faxed to the employer.

Twisted the right ankle stepping off a curb 6 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.
Vitamin D came back 18. Started 1000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.

Mole on the upper back that her spouse noticed. About 7 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.
Message from the patient about scheduling. Wants a date in the next couple of months if the insurance comes through. Passed to the scheduler.
Reviewed the psychological evaluation. Scheduling the trial. Anticoagulation and infection precautions reviewed. Vitals today 129 over 77, pulse 75.

Here with a cough and congestion for 8 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if she gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.
Patient called about a tick bite on the shoulder after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.
Percutaneous trial leads placed at T8 and T9 under fluoroscopy, paresthesia coverage of both legs confirmed. Trial programmed, home with the diary.

Trial day 5: pain down from 8 out of 10 to about 5.5, roughly 30 percent, says it takes the edge off. Activity about the same, still not sleeping well, opioid use unchanged. She wants the permanent implant anyway. Leads removed.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 15 and 15. No ocular pathology noted.
Pre-op for permanent implant. Labs fine, nicotine negative. Consent signed for percutaneous leads and a rechargeable generator in the right upper buttock.

expected.note: The chart raises crit-3 (trial) but does not satisfy it; the mention is a plan, a shortfall, or a result below the threshold.
